# 2 Chronicles Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Jehoshaphat had great wealth and honor, and he allied himself with Ahab through marriage.

**2** Some years later he went to visit Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered large numbers of sheep and cattle for him and his entourage, and persuaded him to join in an attack on Ramoth-gilead.

**3** Ahab king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to attack Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat replied, "I am with you all the way — my people are your people. We'll join you in battle."

**4** But Jehoshaphat added, "First, let's find out what the LORD says."

**5** So the king of Israel gathered four hundred prophets and asked them, "Should we attack Ramoth-gilead, or not?" "Attack!" they said. "God will hand it over to the king."

**6** But Jehoshaphat asked, "Isn't there a prophet of the LORD here we can also consult?"

**7** The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "There is one more man we could ask, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good about me — only bad news. His name is Micaiah son of Imlah." "The king shouldn't say that," Jehoshaphat replied.

**8** So the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once."

**9** The king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah, dressed in their royal robes, were sitting on their thrones at the threshing floor near the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them.

**10** Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made iron horns and declared, "This is what the LORD says: 'With these you will gore the Arameans until they are destroyed.'"

**11** All the other prophets agreed: "Attack Ramoth-gilead and be victorious! The LORD will hand it to the king."

**12** The messenger who went to get Micaiah said to him, "Look, the other prophets are unanimously predicting success for the king. Go along with them and say something favorable."

**13** But Micaiah said, "As surely as the LORD lives, I will say only what my God tells me."

**14** When he arrived before the king, the king asked him, "Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth-gilead, or not?" "Attack and be victorious!" he replied. "They will be handed over to you."

**15** The king said, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the LORD's name?"

**16** Then Micaiah said, "I saw all Israel scattered across the hills like sheep without a shepherd, and the LORD said, 'These people have no master. Let each one go home in peace.'"

**17** The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you? He never prophesies anything good about me — only bad."

**18** Micaiah continued, "Then listen to the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on His throne with all the armies of heaven standing at His right and left.

**19** And the LORD said, 'Who will lure Ahab king of Israel into attacking Ramoth-gilead to his death?' Various suggestions were made.

**20** Finally, a spirit stepped forward, stood before the LORD, and said, 'I will lure him.' 'How?' the LORD asked.

**21** 'I will go and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets,' he said. 'You will succeed,' said the LORD. 'Go and do it.'

**22** So you see — the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours. The LORD has decreed disaster for you."

**23** Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah went up and slapped Micaiah in the face. "Since when did the Spirit of the LORD leave me to speak to you?" he demanded.

**24** Micaiah replied, "You'll find out on the day you go running to hide in an inner room."

**25** The king of Israel ordered, "Arrest Micaiah and send him back to Amon the city governor and to Prince Joash.

**26** Tell them, 'The king says: Put this man in prison and feed him nothing but bread and water until I return safely.'"

**27** Micaiah declared, "If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." Then he added, "Mark my words, all you people!"

**28** So the king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah marched on Ramoth-gilead.

**29** The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "I'll go into battle in disguise, but you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they entered the battle.

**30** Now the king of Aram had ordered his chariot commanders, "Don't fight anyone except the king of Israel himself."

**31** When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they thought, "That's the king of Israel!" They turned to attack him, but Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him. God drew them away from him.

**32** When the chariot commanders realized he wasn't the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him.

**33** But someone drew his bow randomly and hit the king of Israel between the sections of his armor. Ahab told his chariot driver, "Turn around and get me out of the fighting — I've been wounded."

**34** The battle raged all day, and the king of Israel propped himself up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. At sunset, he died.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **18:1**: Jehoshaphat's marriage alliance with Ahab is his defining mistake. Everything good about his reign is now endangered by this partnership with the most corrupt king in Israel's history.

- **18:13**: "I will say only what my God tells me" — Micaiah against four hundred prophets. This is what prophetic courage looks like: one man, one voice, the truth.

- **18:21**: A lying spirit — authorized by God — in the mouths of the prophets. This passage terrifies because it suggests that prophetic unanimity can be divinely orchestrated deception. The only defense is the character of the individual prophet.

- **18:33**: A random arrow kills the king of Israel. Except it wasn't random. Ahab disguised himself to hide from God's judgment. The arrow found him anyway. You can't hide from a sentence God has passed.


— PNEUMA
